common_name: Lisa Ann Bearded Iris (White and Rose-Pink Tangerine-Bearded Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in late summer to early fall with the top surface exposed to the sun in well-drained soil so roots establish before frost.

directions: Registered by Barry Blyth in the late 1970s from a cross of 'Snow Peach' and 'Outer Limits', Lisa Ann carries white standards faintly flushed pink at the midrib over falls that deepen from white to rose-pink at the hafts, set off by a bright tangerine-red beard. It blooms midseason to late on sturdy stalks and became an influential breeding parent in its own right, crossed on to produce 'Tomorrow's Child' among other later introductions. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom, discarding the old woody center and keeping rhizome tops exposed to full sun.
sources: American Iris Society Iris Encyclopedia (Iris Wiki)

common_name: Child of Fortune Bearded Iris (Pink and Rose-Lilac Ruffled Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in late summer to early fall with the top surface exposed to the sun in well-drained soil so roots establish before frost.

directions: Registered by Barry Blyth in 1979 from a cross of 'Sostenique' and 'Venus Magic', Child of Fortune opens pink standards over falls of pink overlaid with rose-lilac, ruffled at the edges and set off by a tangerine-red beard, on a midseason-blooming, well-branched stalk. It went on to become a notable breeding parent, crossed with 'Lisa Ann' to produce 'Tomorrow's Child' among other later introductions. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom, discarding the old woody center and keeping rhizome tops exposed to full sun.
sources: American Iris Society Iris Encyclopedia (Iris Wiki)

common_name: Sea Gold Hosta (Rounded Bright Gold Mildred Seaver Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Sea Gold is one of hybridizer Mildred Seaver's early named golds, forming a tidy mound of medium-sized, rounded, bright gold leaves that hold their color well through the shade-garden season. Near-white, star-shaped flowers rise on scapes in early summer above the foliage mass. It went on to become a notable breeding parent, used as the seed parent with 'Golden Torch' as the pollen parent to produce the giant hosta 'Mississippi Delta'. Plant in moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade and divide congested clumps every few years in spring or fall.

common_name: Golden Torch Hosta (Upright Gold-Leaved Benedict Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade.

directions: Golden Torch is an upright-growing gold hosta from Dr. Benedict's breeding line, carrying bright yellow foliage on a more vertical, torch-like habit than most sprawling gold cultivars, which makes it useful as a vertical accent among lower-growing shade perennials. It serves as the pollen parent, crossed onto 'Sea Gold' as seed parent, in the breeding of the giant hosta 'Mississippi Delta'. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor.

common_name: Victoria Zoysiagrass (NC State Japonica x Matrella Breeding Hybrid)

planting.note: Establish only from sod or plugs (not seed) once soil is consistently above 65F; Victoria is an NC State interspecific breeding hybrid used mainly as parent stock rather than planted directly as a commercial lawn cultivar.

directions: Victoria is a Zoysia japonica x matrella interspecific hybrid developed within North Carolina State University's turfgrass breeding program, combining the coarser texture and cold tolerance of japonica parentage with the finer leaf blade typical of matrella types. It is chiefly significant as breeding stock, having been crossed with 'Meyer' zoysiagrass in 2014 to produce the NC State release 'Lobo', registered as 'XZ 14069' and commercialized in 2021. Where planted directly, establish only from sod or plugs, irrigate closely during the slow zoysia establishment period, and mow at a low, even height once rooted in. It performs best in the warm-season transition zone and milder climates to the south.
sources: Milla-Lewis et al., Journal of Plant Registrations, 'Registration of XZ 14069 Zoysiagrass'

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring into strongly acidic, peaty, constantly moist bog soil topped with a sand layer, mimicking commercial cranberry bog conditions.

directions: Prolific originated as an elite wild-selected cranberry from Michigan bogs around 1900 and was carried forward chiefly as breeding stock rather than for direct commercial production. Crossed with 'McFarlin' in 1961, it produced 'Crowley', a cultivar bred specifically for processing use, and the hybrid offspring are noted for higher anthocyanin content than either parent alone. Grow it under the same strongly acidic, constantly moist bog culture, winter flooding, and sanding regimen used for other cranberry selections. It remains mostly of interest to heirloom collectors and breeding programs tracing the lineage of modern processing cranberries.
